subject.title: [Feature] Cron and subagent sessions lack user context for plugin OAuth tools

question: What requester identity contract should cron and subagent runs expose to plugin OAuth tools?
rationale: This would let unattended or delegated execution act under a user OAuth identity, so automation cannot safely choose the API shape, authority boundary, consent model, or audit semantics.

options.title: Typed Gateway/Plugin SDK Requester Context
options.body: Add a runtime-owned requester identity seam propagated only from approved schedule/spawn authority, with consent, audit, revocation, and privacy rules.

options.title: Plugin-Local Default Identity Only
options.body: Keep core unchanged and let affected plugins define explicit scheduled identities where their owners can enforce plugin-specific OAuth policy.

options.title: No User-Scoped OAuth For Unattended Runs
options.body: Keep cron and spawned sessions headless for user OAuth tools unless they are triggered by an active inbound user message.

recommendation.title: Typed Gateway/Plugin SDK Requester Context
recommendation.body: Add a runtime-owned requester identity seam propagated only from approved schedule/spawn authority, with consent, audit, revocation, and privacy rules.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined feature-history signal across cron agent binding, sessions_spawn, and subagent runtime boundaries.
